rationale:
Evidence. The best raced design is iteration 1 (score 158.144): kp 3.0, ki 0.4, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.6, outer sensors at x = ±0.04, sensor_size 0.016. Every later single-variable change lowered the score. Lowering base_speed to 1.2 (iteration 2) cut oval finishes from 5/20 to 0/20. Widening the outer sensors to ±0.06 (iteration 3) dropped the score to 54.9 and removed all oval finishes. Raising kp to 3.5 (iteration 4) gave 108.2 and cut oval finishes to 1/20. Across all raced designs, max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.063 m against the 0.06 m off-track limit, steering oscillation is low (0.11 to 0.28), and the s-bend and slalom fail at progress 0.09 to 0.17. The failure is therefore drift into bends, not jitter, and more proportional authority made it worse.

Evaluator note. The Evaluator's approved entityR1 (kp 3.5, outer sensors ±0.04, all else as iteration 1) is identical to the iteration 4 design, which has already raced and scored 108.24. I am not resubmitting it, because it is a known worse design and its feedback predates the iteration 4 result.

Change. I keep iteration 1 as the base and make one change: kd from 0.3 to 0.5. The hypothesis (H4) is that the robot overshoots each bend and then leaves the tape on the far side, so more derivative damping should reduce overshoot without the extra proportional gain that hurt in iteration 4. Steering oscillation is low, so the added damping should not be limited by jitter.

Expected result. Progress on s-bend and slalom above about 0.2, max_error below about 0.06 m, and the oval finish rate at least 0.25. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, damping is adding noise and kd should return to 0.3. If progress is unchanged, the next test is ki 0.8 (the remaining steady offset) or a seven-sensor layout with inner sensors at x = ±0.03.
